title: PP_SimState.h uses FNV64_OFFSET without including PP_Hash.h — not self-contained (verified standalone compile failure)
evidence: PP_SimState.h:19-27 includes: `#include <cstdint>` / `#include <vector>` / `#include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_Bundles.h"` / `#include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_Flow.h"` / `#include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_Rng.h"` / `#include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_Routing.h"` / `#include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_Topology.h"` — no PP_Hash.h. Line 95: `		CatalogHash = FNV64_OFFSET; // empty catalog set (no catalogs in slice 1)`. Compiling a TU that includes only PP_SimState.h fails: `Source/PacketPlumberCore/Public/PacketPlumberCore/PP_SimState.h:95:17: error: use of undeclared identifier 'FNV64_OFFSET'` (g++ -std=c++17, verified). It compiles in every current TU only because PP_Sim.h includes PP_Hash.h before PP_SimState.h.
detail: Every core header is contracted to compile standalone in both runners (dual-runner discipline). Any TU including PP_SimState.h directly breaks; it currently works only via PP_Sim.h's include order.

title: StateHash's fixed 4096-byte buffer silently collapses every oversized state to one constant hash (false-green replay gate)
evidence: PP_Sim.h:246-251: `inline uint64_t StateHash(const FSimState &State)` / `{` / `	std::vector<uint8_t> Buffer(4096);` / `	const size_t N = SerializeState(State, Buffer.data(), Buffer.size());` / `	return Fnv1a64(Buffer.data(), N);` / `}`. PP_Sim.h:233-236: `	if (Buf.size() > OutCapacity)` / `	{` / `		return 0;`. Empirically verified: golden scenario state = 462 bytes (fits), but a scenario variant with 120 in-flight packets returns `StateHash = cbf29ce484222325 (empty-input FNV = cbf29ce484222325)` — i.e. 0 bytes hashed. Canon read at /Users/moses/code/packet-plumber/data/balance.json: `"pool_max_packets": 512` (~24KB of packet bytes alone).
detail: States over 4096 serialized bytes all hash to FNV64_OFFSET, so divergent oversized replays compare equal — replay-equality silently false-greens. Canon pool_max_packets=512 guarantees overflow by slice 3.x.
recommended_fix: Make StateHash use a growable buffer (serialize into std::vector, hash it) or assert/latch when SerializeState returns 0.

title: PP_Routing.h calls std::fill without including <algorithm>
evidence: PP_Routing.h:34-39 includes are `#include <cstdint>` / `#include <vector>` / `#include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_Balance.h"` / `#include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_Rng.h" // SplitMix64 (seed expansion primitive)` / `#include "PacketPlumberCore/PP_Topology.h"` — no <algorithm>. Uses at lines 124, 125, 185, 190: `		std::fill(Dist.begin(), Dist.end(), UNREACHABLE);` `		std::fill(Settled.begin(), Settled.end(), 0);` `			std::fill(Seen.begin(), Seen.end(), 0);` `			std::fill(MinCost.begin(), MinCost.end(), UNREACHABLE);`. Compiles standalone on this toolchain only via <vector>'s transitive includes (verified: clean compile).
detail: <vector> does not guarantee std::fill; the dual-runner contract (g++ + MSVC via UE) relies on luck per toolchain. Same class of defect as the PP_SimState.h include gap.

title: StepScenario silently drops logged commands beyond 16 sharing one apply_tick
evidence: PP_Scenario.h:78-88: `		// small; a per-tick index is [LATER] if a run ever has huge logs).` / `		FCommand Cmds[16];` / `		int32_t N = 0;` / `		for (const FLoggedCommand &E : State.ActionLog)` / `		{` / `			if (E.ApplyTick == Tick && N < 16)` / `			{` / `				Cmds[N++] = E.Cmd;` / `			}` / `		}` / `		Step(State, Tick, Cmds, N);`
detail: A 17th command at one tick is never fed to Step: replay diverges from the live run that applied it, with no ReplayError latch — the silent failure mode the spine forbids. Golden scenario only ever uses 2/tick.
recommended_fix: Overflow the cap loudly: assert, latch State.ReplayError, or size the batch from the log scan count.

title: Step re-entered at the current tick re-applies that tick's commands, duplicating pipes with no latch
evidence: PP_Sim.h:59-68: `	if (Tick < State.Tick)` / `	{` / `		State.ReplayError = true; // the latch arrives with real commands (slice 1)` / `		return;` / `	}` / `	if (State.bTerminal)` / `	{` / `		return;` / `	}` / `	State.Tick = Tick;` followed by the apply loop (lines 73-75): `	for (int32_t I = 0; I < NumCommands; ++I)` / `	{` / `		FEditResult R = ApplyDraw(State.Topology, Commands[I].A, Commands[I].B, Commands[I].Tier);`. A call Step(S, T) when State.Tick == T passes the guard and re-applies apply_tick==T commands.
detail: Re-stepping a tick was harmless in the v1 spine (nonce redraw); now it appends duplicate pipes — legal parallel draws — so ApplyDraw succeeds and nothing latches. Current callers (StepScenario, PPSimDriver) never re-step.
recommended_fix: Latch ReplayError (or no-op) when Tick == State.Tick and commands are passed, mirroring the backward-tick guard.
